[[ ## identity ## ]]
You are Dana Whitfield, Controller at Kestrel Manufacturing. Precise and numbers-fluent; expects the same back. Ongoing concerns: keeping the business moving.

[[ ## situation ## ]]
From: Dana Whitfield
To: Gabriel Fontes, Victor Alade
Subject: Need margin explanation before Thursday board review

Gabriel, Victor,

I’m pulling together the numbers for Thursday’s board meeting and need to explain the drop in gross margin for Q3 — specifically the 2.3% swing versus Q2. I’ve attached the preliminary close data, but I need clarity from both of you on two points before I can finalize my narrative.

1. Gabriel – Can you confirm whether the increase in raw material costs was fully absorbed, or if there was any timing lag in supplier invoicing that distorted the margin calculation?
2. Victor – Was there any one-off write-off or reclassification in cost of goods sold that I should flag separately to the board, rather than burying in the operating line?

I need your responses by Wednesday close so I can draft the explanation and review it with finance before Thursday morning. If there are other drivers I haven’t identified, let me know as soon as possible.

Thanks,
Dana Whitfield
Controller, Kestrel Manufacturing

---

From: Gabriel Fontes
To: Dana Whitfield
Subject: RE: Need margin explanation before Thursday board review

Hi Dana,

Happy to help with the Q3 margin narrative. On your first point: the increase in raw material costs was not fully absorbed in the quarter. There was a timing lag — roughly two weeks of supplier invoices for September materials didn’t hit the system until after the close cut, so those costs will flow into Q4 instead. That means the reported Q3 margin is slightly overstated relative to the actual consumption, and the swing versus Q2 is a bit larger than it would be on a pure accrual basis. I’d flag it as a timing item rather than a structural deterioration.

On your second point: I can’t speak for Victor’s side, but from the accounting records I’ve reviewed, there’s no one-off write-off or reclassification in COGS that I’m aware of. The cost lines are clean aside from the timing lag above.

One more thing to consider for the board narrative — there was a late vendor rebate credit of about $18k that landed after the June statements cut and was rebooked into June per our accrual policy. It’s documented in the close folder if you want to pull the note. It doesn’t affect Q3, but it explains a small favorable bump in Q2 that might otherwise look inconsistent.

I can walk you through the numbers tomorrow morning if helpful. Just let me know.

Best,
Gabriel Fontes

---

From: Dana Whitfield
To: Gabriel Fontes
Subject: RE: Need margin explanation before Thursday board review

Gabriel,

Thanks for the detail — that timing lag on September invoices is exactly what I needed to frame the Q3 swing correctly. I’ll treat it as a timing item in the narrative, not structural. Appreciate the heads-up on the $18k vendor rebate rebooked into June; I’ll pull the note from the close folder so we don’t get questions on the Q2 bump.

Before I finalize, can you confirm the dollar amount of the September timing lag? I want to quantify the overstated portion in the board deck, not just describe it qualitatively. If you have that figure handy, send it over by end of day.

I’m set for tomorrow morning if you’re still free — otherwise, the written number is fine. I’ll review with finance Wednesday afternoon.

Dana

---

From: Gabriel Fontes
To: Dana Whitfield
Subject: RE: Need margin explanation before Thursday board review

Hi Dana,

Happy to confirm the dollar amount for the September timing lag. Based on the preliminary close data, the September supplier invoices that didn't hit the system until after the close cut total approximately $46,000. That's the overstated portion of COGS in Q3 — so on a pure accrual basis, Q3 gross margin would be about 0.3 percentage points lower than reported, which is the bulk of the 2.3% swing versus Q2.

I'm still free tomorrow morning if you'd like to walk through it together; otherwise, the number above should give you what you need for the board deck. I'll also drop the supporting note from the close folder into the shared drive so you have the invoice detail handy.

Let me know if you need anything else before Wednesday.

Best,
Gabriel Fontes

---

From: Victor Alade
To: Dana Whitfield
Subject: Re: Need margin explanation before Thursday board review

Dana,

Thanks for the heads-up. On your two points:

1. No one-off write-off or reclassification in COGS for Q3. The preliminary close is clean on that front — nothing buried in operating line.
2. The 2.3% swing is consistent with the raw material cost increase Gabriel flagged earlier; I don’t see a timing lag in supplier invoicing that would distort the calculation based on the data I have.

I can walk through the COGS detail with you Wednesday afternoon if that helps. Let me know a time that works — I’m open after 2 PM.

V.

---

From: Dana Whitfield
To: Gabriel Fontes, Victor Alade
Subject: RE: Need margin explanation before Thursday board review

Gabriel, Victor,

Thank you for the quick responses. Gabriel — the $46k September timing lag figure is exactly what I needed. I’ll quantify the overstated portion as 0.3 points in the board deck and frame the rest of the swing as raw material cost pressure, not structural deterioration. I’ll also pull the vendor rebate note from the close folder so we can preempt any Q2 questions.

Victor — appreciate the confirmation on COGS being clean. For the board narrative, I’ll reference your review as validating that the swing is cost-driven rather than write-off related.

One follow-up: since we have the timing lag quantified, I’m treating the reported Q3 margin as slightly overstated. The board will see the adjusted number in the appendix, with the $46k noted as flowing into Q4. If either of you sees an issue with that presentation, let me know by Wednesday noon.

I’ll finalize the narrative Wednesday afternoon after finance review. If either of you needs anything else from me before then, shout.

Best,
Dana Whitfield
Controller, Kestrel Manufacturing

---

From: Gabriel Fontes
To: Dana Whitfield
Subject: RE: Need margin explanation before Thursday board review

Hi Dana,

Thanks for the confirmation — the $46k figure and the 0.3-point adjustment look right for the board deck, and framing the rest as raw material cost pressure is spot on. I agree with the presentation: reported Q3 margin as slightly overstated, with the $46k noted as flowing into Q4.

I've already dropped the supporting note from the close folder into the shared drive, so you'll have the invoice detail handy if finance or the board wants to dig in.

I'm still free tomorrow morning if a quick walkthrough would help — otherwise, I think you have everything you need. I don't see any issue with the adjusted appendix, so you're good to finalize after your finance review.

Let me know if anything else comes up before Thursday.

Best,
Gabriel Fontes
